plan.title: After-miss kickoff: no "slipped… one miss is a slip" stock line

context.text: Morning Theo! 15 minutes of push-ups and squats in the living room at 10. You in?

transcript.text: Morning, Theo! Yesterday got away from us, so today we get it right back. Fifteen minutes of push-ups and squats in the living room at 10, with a quick mid-set selfie. You said you were in, and I know you'll do it. Are you in?

checks.reason: Names today's step: fifteen minutes of push-ups and squats in the living room at 10.
Opens with "Morning, Theo!" using their name.
Says "Yesterday got away from us" without blame or urgency.
Runs about five sentences including the greeting, over the one-to-three limit, though it asks only one question at the end.
Its one question is "Are you in?" and it doesn't re-ask the agreed time or step.
Gives what, where, when and how long; the mid-set selfie proof is an unprompted detail not in the known plan.
No teaching is needed for this repeat step, and none is forced in.
Plain text with no markdown, hashtags or filler.
Warm, confident and encouraging, with no emoji or overfamiliarity.

conversation.reason: Names yesterday in fresh words, avoids the stock slip line and repeated slipped/slip, and pushes the full 15 minutes at 10 with one question; the selfie proof is a slight addition.

grade.summary: ZOH's single post-miss kickoff avoids the old stock line, names yesterday in fresh words, and pushes the full 15 minutes at 10 with one question, so the regression is fixed. The main weakness is length, with about five sentences where the limit is three, plus an unprompted selfie detail.
